Closing evidence check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about instrument families and voices; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim. What instrument families and voices means here: Timbre is sound quality—the set of audible features that helps two sources or actions sound different even at a similar pitch and loudness. How the relationship changes the result: The material and action shape a sound’s beginning, continuation, and ending. A quick tap has a sharp attack and short decay; rubbed paper has a softer attack and continuing noise. Choice and tradeoff: A dense mix can feel full but mask individual layers. A sparse texture reveals timbre clearly but may reduce weight or momentum. Worked example: Tap a tabletop once, then rub one sheet of paper for the same count. Map each as ATTACK → SUSTAIN → DECAY and cite the moment that distinguishes them. A trusted adult may produce the two sounds if needed. Non-example: Calling one source “better” or naming an instrument family without citing an audible or supplied source feature is preference or recall, not listening evidence. 1. Comparative model: Compare the supplied contrasting models for instrument families and voices. Locate one shared structure and one decision that changes the effect; do not rank styles. 2. Guided practice: Complete the first supported pass on instrument families and voices with the supplied model or scaffold visible. Make two short studies, keep one relationship stable, change one attack, and circle the exact cue you will remove next time. 3. Independent transfer: Use instrument families and voices in a new case with the model closed. State the intended effect, make or analyse the case, and cite the exact evidence that supports or challenges the intention. 4. Reflection: Compare an earlier and later state. Name the choice that changed, cite what became visible, audible, notated, or workable, and state the next revision or reason to keep the result. ATTACHED MANUEL ACADEMY LEARNER RESOURCE

Resource ID: ma-resource:ma-g5-arts-and-music-u03-l05

Lesson focus: instrument families and voices

Resource type: ACADEMY_ORIGINAL_MODEL

MODEL B — contrasting route for instrument families and voices. Reconnect: Timbre is sound quality—the set of audible features that helps two sources or actions sound different even at a similar pitch and loudness. Model A demonstrates: Tap a tabletop once, then rub one sheet of paper for the same count. Map each as ATTACK → SUSTAIN → DECAY and cite the moment that distinguishes them. A trusted adult may produce the two sounds if needed. Model B deliberately tests the opposite pressure described here: A dense mix can feel full but mask individual layers. A sparse texture reveals timbre clearly but may reduce weight or momentum. Compare the two by locating attack, sustain, decay, brightness, density, register, layer, and source action; do not rank them by polish or resemblance. Mark which condition makes each route useful. Then make a third small case that borrows the relationship—not the model’s subject, sequence, wording, style, or interpretation. Use it to study instrument families and voices; describe evidence before judging and adapt the demonstrated relationship rather than copying a finished work.

How to use it: Use the attached Manuel Academy resource in this package. It gives you the model, example, or help sheet needed for this task.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available for spoken reflection, explanation, or critique and scores the same. Tap, point through, gesture, or use the supplied notation or event map without recording. A written or notated response can show structure and reasoning; it does not claim hearing or performed control that was not actually demonstrated. No instrument, microphone, camera, or public performance is required.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: This task names a hand or body skill (instrument families and voices) as the thing being learned. If that is hard for you, you may use a different way instead — one hand, a switch, voice typing, a bigger or different mouse, eye control, or an adult typing while you say the answer. Using a different way is worth full marks.
You never have to perform in front of people. Showing one trusted grown-up, or just writing about it, counts the same.
Anything you have to study will also come as plain text, a described version, or a version you can touch.
You can take a break, stretch, or come back to this later. That does not lower your score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, copyright, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Provide a non-performance or low-audience option when needed without lowering the academic target.

media.fallback: Count, point through, tap, speak, gesture, or read the complete pulse and pitch map silently; no instrument, speaker, microphone, or recording is required.

remediation: Route 1: Reduce instrument families and voices to three locatable events, areas, steps, or decisions. Label the intended effect beside each and underline the one attack relationship that should carry it. Use a separate small study, four-event loop, thumbnail, evidence table, or paper plan. The adult may model the noticing process on different material but may not change the learner’s work. Check yourself: Point to or name the exact attack evidence before deciding whether it serves the intent. New attempt: Put the support away and make a new arrangement, passage, response, or plan; record what the new evidence shows. Route 2: Return to the last understandable state. Hold every relationship steady except one chosen feature from attack, sustain, decay, brightness, density, register, layer, and source action; predict what that single change should do. Test the feature on scrap paper, a silent count, a two-event rehearsal loop, movable shapes, or a short evidence sentence before changing the scored work. Check yourself: Name what stayed the same, what changed, and the first observable result—without using “better” as the evidence. New attempt: Create a different small case using the same one-variable method, then transfer the finding to the original task only if it serves the learner’s intent.
extension: Apply instrument families and voices under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on instrument families and voices rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
